minutes_text:
CITY  OF SOUTH  GATE
  REGULAR  CITY  COUNCIL  MEETING
  MINUTES
  TUESDAY,  JUNE  10, 2025

CALL  TO ORDER  Maria  Davila,  Mayor  called  a Regular  City  Council  Meeting  to order at
  7:02 p.m.

INVOCATION  Steve Costley,  Director  Parks & Recreation

PLEDGE  OFALLEGIANCE  Jose De La Paz, City  Treasurer

ROLL  CALL  Yodit  Glaze,  City  Clerk

PRESENT  Mayor  Maria  Davila,  Vice  Mayor  Joshua Barron,  Council  Member  Maria
  del Pilar Avalos,  Council  Member  Gil Hurtado  and Council  Member  Al
  Rios;  City  Treasurer  Jose De La Paz, City  Manager  Rob Houston,  City
  Attorney  Raul F. Salinas

COMMENTS  FROM  THE
AUDIENCE  (NON-AGENDA

ITEMS)  Mario  Dominguez  is requesting  the City  Council  place an item on the
  agenda to change  the email  fees, having  to do with  public  records  request,
  specifically  Fair Political  Practices  Commission  (FPPC).

  Lizette  Ruiz,  Kauffman  Ave, thanked  the City  Council  for speaking  out
  and being  involved  in meetings  with  different  government  officials  form
  the state regarding  the ICE raids.  She also believes  the budget  item should
  have been heard earlier  in the meeting.

  Francisco  Gallegos,  Otis Street,  is concerned  about the illegal  fireworks  in
  this community.

  Rubin  Pichardo,  long-time  South  Gate resident,  is present  tonight  to
  clarify  certain  comments  made by Vice Mayor  Barron.

  Javier,  South  Gate resident,  is asking  for clarification  on the city's  stance
  regarding  ICE.

  Osvaldo  Pichardo,  San Gabriel  Ave, is present  tonight  to clarify  cornrnents
  made by Vice  Mayor  Barron  and Council  Member  Hurtado.

  Alice,  South  Gate resident,  is concerned  that people  show up at Council
  Meetings  and are accusing  the current  City  Council  Members  of fraud.
  Her complaint  is with  the Parks Department  because  she cannot  attend  the
  weight  control  meetings  because  they are only  in Spanish.
   REGULAR  CITY  COUNCIL  MEETING  MINUTES  OF JUNE  10, 2025

COMMENTS  FROM  THE
AUDIENCE  (NON-AGENDA

ITEMS)  CONT'D  Cecilia  Caballero,  South  Gate resident,  owns  a company  for multilingual
  books  for children.  She mentioned  a literacy  festival  for this summer.  She

  received  a call from  a good friend  that was planning  a pride  festival  but

  got turned  down.  She's present  tonight  supporting  him.

  Adolfo  Varas,  South  Gate resident,  was a keynote  speaker  at a graduation
  in the City of Bell. He stated it took him five years to advocate for his
  LGBTQ+  community  to declare the month of June as Pride Month. He
  stated establishing  a Pride Festival  that shows  unity,  love,  education,  and

  resources.  He thanked  Councilwoman  Avalos  and every  elected  official

  throughout  the southeast  Los Angeles  region,  multiple  different  cities

  reaching  out, wanting  his Pride  Festival.  He hopes the City  Clerk  will  read

  the emails  and not give a summary.  He is asking  the City  Council  to

  continue  supporting  the LGBTQ+  community.

  Laura  thanked  everyone  for their  support.  She is the Membership  Director

  for the City  of Bell  Chamber  of Commerce.  She stated the Pride  Festival  is

  to provide  resources  for the youth  that do not have anywhere  to go.

  Vince,  SELA  Pride  Festiva  Chair,  and resident  of the cities  of San Pedro

  and Paramount.  He stated his first Pride Festival  was hosted  in the City  of

  South  Gate.

  Miguel  Angel  Alvarez  Godinez,  LA County  Commissioner  on HIV,  and is

  present  tonight  in support  of the SELA  Pride  Festival.  He would  like this
  city to support  its citizens.

  Ezequiel  Flores,  South  Gate resident,  and reiterated  what his other
  colleagues  have stated.

EMAILS  Ed Rod expressing  disappointment  with  the City  of South  Gate's  decision

  to withdraw  from  participating  in the SELA  Pride.  He is urging  the city to

  consider  its decision,  stating  that pulling  back sends a harmful  message,
  especially  to the youth.

  Tenaya,  South  Gate resident  and SELA  Pride  attendee,  is expressing
  concern  about the city's  recent  decision  to withdraw  from  hosting  this

  year's  pride  She emphasized
  event.  South  Gate needs pride  celebration  to

  support  its peer residents and allies.

  Sophie  Ryan,  South  Gate resident,  expresses  appreciation  for the city's

  ongoing  efforts  to be a safe and inclusive  space and special  thanks  to Mr.

  Costley  for his long-standing  support  and student  events  over the past
  decades.  Ms. Ryan is asking Council to review  the proposal  and consider
  the possibility of hosting the event this summer.

COMMENTS  FROM  THE
AUDIENCE  (NON-AGF.NDA

ITEMS)  CONT'D  EMAILS  Miss Ady  Cortez  in response  to a social  media  post by Adolfo  Varas
  regarding  the city's  involvement  in the SELA  Pride Festival.  She states
  that one of Mr. Vara's  staff members  dropped  off the event application  on
  Wednesday,  June 4'h and later reviewed  and corrected  by her mother
  before  being  submitted  on Thursday,  June 5fll. She added that he had
  previously  been informed  that the application  should  have been submitted
  3 to 6 months  prior  to the event.  She concluded  by saying  it is unfair  to
  spread misinformation  and that doing  so reflects  poorly  on the LGBTQ
  community.

  Miss  Jennifer  Daly,  on behalf  of Ruben  Pichardo  and several  concerned
  residents  regarding  the city's  code enforcement  practices,  alleging  that
  South  Gate residents  are being  unfairly  cited for minor  or unfounded
  violations  while  large commercial  entities  are allowed  to operate  without
  proper  permits  or enforcement.

  Miss  Martha  Torres,  Community  Engagement  Liaison  with  the Fair
  Housing  Foundation,  informing  the city about the free services  the
  organization  provides  to South  Gate residents.

REPORTS  AND  COMMENTS

FROM  CITY  OFFICIALS  Rob Houston,  City  Manager  stated that regarding  the city's  support  of
  pride  community  and Pride Festival,  the city has a history  from  both City
  Council  and staff to support  the cornrnunity  and has had past pride
  festivals.  He stated the city has a set of rules and regulations  to make sure
  all the community  members  want to do events  in the park.

  Mayor  Davila  stated the City  of South  Gate was the first to have the Pride
  Festival  during  Covid.  She stated there is a process  and regulations  that
  need to be followed.

  Mayor  Davila  stated she has LGBTQ  family  members  and is a big
  supporter  of the LGBTQ  community.  She also informed  the public  that the
  Proclamation  for Pride  Month  is at the next Council  Meeting.

  Arturo  Cervantes,  Director  of Public  Works,  reported  construction  on the
  residential  resurfacing  project.

  Steve Costley,  Director  of Parks & Recreation,  stated the park is very
  busy. He mentioned  the registration  for classes has started  for the summer
  quarter.

  Gabriel  Perez, Director  of Community  Development,  stated staff is
  working  on a fagade  improvement  program  for Tweedy  Boulevard.

  Page 3 of 8
   REGULAR  CITY  COUNCIL  MEETING  MINUTES  OF JUNE  10, 2025

REPORTS  AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS

CONT'D  Luis  Frausto,  Director  of Administrative  Services,  stated that for a couple
  of meetings  we have had technical  issues with  the streaming  services.

  Staff take this very  seriously  and have resources  that have been dedicated
  to troubleshooting  and ensuring  the connection  was stable.

  Jon Hamilton,  Director  of Human  Resources,  has nothing  to report.  He

  wished  everybody  Happy  Father's  Day.

  Darren  Arakawa,  Chief  of Police,  stated there isn't  a real solution  to the

  fireworks.  He agrees staff is an issue. He mentioned  the citation  fees. He

  mentioned  the street fair was well attended without  any issues.

  The Chief  was on a conference call regarding  irnrnigration  with the LAPD

  Chief and Sheriff with the 45 Police Chiefs about what we are doing
  locally within the communities.  He has a profound  respect for the law. It is
  agreed in law enforcement  that there is a big gap in communication  with

  the federal govemment.  The Chief stated that the federal government  does

  not need anyone's permission  to come into the community.  There  is no

  mandate  that they community  with  the cities.

  Rob Houston,  City  Manager  stated everyone  has the right  for peaceful

  protesting  that's  encouraged  in our democratic  society  and supported  by

  the police,  council  and staff. But if the protesting  creates vandalism  or

  aggression  that will be addressed  like any  other  law.

  Raul F. Salinas,  City Attorney  had nothing  to report.

  Jose De La Paz, City  Treasurer,  will  save his time on the proposed  budget

  item.

  Yodit  Glaze,  City  Clerk,  spoke on the summarized  email  comments.  She

  also spoke on the fee resolution Mr. Dominguez  brought  up. She wished
  everybody  a Happy Father's Day.

  Council  Member  Avalos  thanked  the cornrnunity  and appreciated  the

  compliments  by the Pichardo  family.  She acknowledges  the South Gate

  families  that are afraid  to leave their homes,  go to work,  take their children

  to school  or the park. She's made a few social  media  posts if anyone  needs

  resources, to reach out to her.

  Council  Member  Avalos  attended  the Southeast  Water  Coalition  and on

  April  9fh it was indicated  the water  rates were going  to increase  by 4%.

  The Budget  Advisory  Committee  indicated  that it was not needed. The
  water increased  by 3.8. She also attended  the Men's Health, but a lot of the
  community  leaders did not attend, and she understands  the reason.  She

  wished  all the fathers  a Happy  Father's  Day.

  Page 4 of 8

REPORTS  AND  COMMENTS
FROM  CITY  OFFICIALS

CONT'D  Council  Member  Avalos  is concerned  and disappointment  regarding
  Council  Member  Hurtado's  comtnents  referring  to a colleague.  She is
  demanding  this Council  act through  censure  or mandatory  training.  She is
  asking  for a public  apology.  Since she got on Council,  she has never
  spoken  ill will of anyone in public  because  she holds  herself  at a higher
  standard.

  Council  Member  Hurtado  stated that he never  said any profanity  about  any
  colleague.  At the request  of Mr. Pichardo,  Council  Member  Hurtado
  visited  him over a code enforcement  issue. He informed  Mr. Pichardo  that
  he was not ready to make any decision  as to whether  Mr. Pichardo  got
  cited properly  or not. He would  forward  it to the City  Manager  for his
  review.  Mr. Pichardo  never  asked Council  Member  Hurtado  for anything.

  Council  Member  Hurtado  stated attending  a training  session  at the
  Western  States Carpenters  Union.  He attended  Cal State Dominguez  in
  2017 and 2019 to get a degree  and one of the courses  he took  was Queer
  Studies.  He had a nephew  that was part of the LGBTQ  community.  He and
  his colleagues  have always  been respectful  and supportive  of the LGBTQ
  community  events.

  Council  Member  Hurtado  stated attending  meetings  with  local  leaders
  from  the southeast  area regarding  the ICE issues. He asked the public  to be
  careful  what is posted  on social  media.

  Council  Member  Rios thanked  everyone  present  tonight.  He supports  the
  LGBTQ  community  and understands  the firework  issues. He attended  the
  Men's  Health  fair. He stated that the natives  of this country  are the
  American  Indians.  Everyone  else came from  somewhere.  It is okay to
  protest,  but peacefully.

  Vice Mayor  Barron  asked if the firework  fees can be increased  to deter the
  use of them.

  Chief  Arakawa  responded  that it's City  Councils  decision.  The fines  are
  high already.

  Vice Mayor  Barron  is willing  to discuss  increasing  the firework  fees.

  Chief  Arakawa  stated many  cannot  pay the fines  or it gets appealed.  The
  first  start would  be to ban fireworks.

  Vice Mayor  Barron  questioned  the reason the SWAT  truck  during  the
  street fair.

  Page 5 of 8
   REGULAR  CITY  COUNCIL  MEETING  MINUTES  OF JUNE  10, 2025

REPORTS  AND  COMMENTS
FROM  CITY  OFFICIALS

CONT'D  Chief  Arakawa  stated the SWAT  truck  would  be driving  through  the alleys,
  and it is taken out to cornrnunity events. The SWAT  truck  is a military
  vehicle. ICE does not drive military  vehicles.

  Vice  Mayor  Barron  stated they need to be the eyes to be able to inform the
  residents  of what's  going on. The news will show violence, fires but not
  peace'ful  protests.  He attended  meetings  with  local  leaders  regarding  ICE
  ISSueS.

  Mayor  Davila  attended  several  graduations,  the Centennial  Celebration  for
  San Gabriel  Avenue,  Victoria  Elementary  School  and ribbon  cutting  for
  the Tweedy  Boulevard.

  Mayor  Davila  spoke on the ICE issues and the resources.

  The City  Council  recessed  at 8:45 p.m.,  and reconvened  at 8:53 p.m.,  with
RECESS

  all Members  of Council  present.

DEVIATE  FROM

THE  AGENDA  At this time,  there being  no objections,  Mayor  Davila  stated that item  6
  would  be considered  out of its regular  agenda  order.

LANDSCAPING  The City  Council  approved  items A & B during  Consent  Calendar::

  a.  Purchase  Orders  for Los Angeles  County  Public  Works  to perform
  bridge  maintenance  services  on four city-owned  bridges,  for a
  cumulative  amount  of $117,020  plus a 10%  contingency  of $12,000
  for a total not to exceed  the amount  of $129,020;  and

  b.  Appropriated  $200,000  from  Proposition  C Funds to CIP Project  No.
  719-ST  to fully  fund these four Purchase  Orders  and one other
  Purchase  Order  for bridge  maintenance  that was previously  approved
  by the City  Council  on December  10, 2024.

4

  from  the Southeast  Gateway  Line  Light  Rail  Project  to the Garfield
  Avenue  Complete  Street Improvements,  City  Project  No. 564-ST,  to fully
  fund  services  rendered  for the completion  of construction  during  Consent
  Calendar.

  a.  An excess workers'  insurance  policy  with  Safety  National,  through

  policy  issued  by Safety  National;  and

  c.  Authorized  the Mayor  to execute  the "Request  to Bind  Coverage"  in a
  form  acceptable  to the City Attorney.
